title: Danish study points to reasons for rise in ADHD and autism diagnoses
seoTitle: Study explains rise in ADHD and autism diagnoses
subtitle: New research shows children diagnosed today resemble the general population more than a decade ago
excerpt: Large Danish study suggests the increase in ADHD and autism diagnosis rates may reflect changes in identification patterns.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A substantial study conducted in Denmark provides new insights into the recent and pronounced rise in ADHD and autism diagnoses among children. The research indicates that children diagnosed today exhibit characteristics much more similar to their peers in the general population than those who received the same diagnosis a decade ago.

This shift in clinical profile suggests that the surge in diagnosis rates may be partly linked to broader identification and changes in diagnostic practices, rather than solely to a real increase in the underlying conditions among the child population.

The Danish investigation compares data from different periods and highlights the evolution in how these conditions are recognized and diagnosed today, opening space for new discussions on the topic within the medical and scientific communities.

With information from ScienceDaily.
